The header asserts that modern docker compose resolves each -f file's relative paths against that file's own directory rather than the invoking cwd, and that layering with fully-qualified paths from the repo root 'has been verified to resolve correctly'. release-deploy TESTED the claim rather than accepting it, on Compose v5.1.2 with Docker Engine 29.4.0: from the repo root with fully-qualified -f paths, and again from /private/tmp with absolute -f paths, the sources resolved to the correct /.../deploy/docker/prometheus-observability.yml and /.../docs/prometheus in BOTH cases. So the claim is correct as written. The defect is only that the word 'modern' names no version, on a behaviour that genuinely did change across Compose generations - so an operator on an older Compose cannot tell whether the guidance applies to them, and the failure would be a confusing path-resolution error rather than anything silent. FIX: state 'Compose >= v2.20 (verified on v5.1.2)' rather than 'modern'.
classification_rationale: the version boundary for a version-dependent behaviour claim is absent; the claim itself was executed and holds

trigger: The overlay is applied to the UAT rig, which publishes 9090 on 0.0.0.0; an unauthenticated caller reaches the lifecycle API.
summary: THE DEPLOY-SIDE ANSWER TO sec5-2, INCLUDING AN ENDORSEMENT OF THE MECHANISM THE HEADER CHOSE. release-deploy confirmed by EXECUTION what Gate 2 derived by reading: an unauthenticated POST /-/reload against the running overlay returns 200, and docker-compose.uat.yml:16-17 publishes 9090:9090 on all interfaces. Two agents in two different gates reached this independently. The deploy judgement release-deploy adds, which Gate 2 could not give: --web.enable-lifecycle IS THE RIGHT MECHANISM and should be kept. The alternative the header rejected - recreating the container to pick up a rules change - would re-evaluate the `volumes:` merge on the base rig, and that is PRECISELY how an operator lands in the reversed-`-f` state that R4-1 exists to prevent. So recreate-to-reload would trade a bounded exposure for the exact silent failure this change was written to fix. The fix is therefore one line and costs nothing in a UAT rig: add `ports: ["127.0.0.1:9090:9090"]` to the overlay, which narrows the bind while keeping lifecycle. release-deploy deliberately recorded IMPACT as I8 for its own gate and deferred the I1 security band to sec5-2 rather than double-counting the same exposure across two gates.
classification_rationale: the loopback bind and the warning are both absent; the exposure itself is verified by an executed unauthenticated reload

trigger: An operator runs docker-compose.full-uat.yml expecting the alert rules to be evaluated; that rig has its own Prometheus with no rule_files: and no overlay.
summary: THE OBSERVABILITY STORY IS HALF-APPLIED ACROSS THE RIGS, AND THAT IS DISCLOSED RATHER THAN CONCEALED. docker-compose.full-uat.yml runs its own Prometheus against prometheus-full-uat.yml, which has no rule_files: and no overlay, so the full-UAT rig evaluates none of the 116 rules. release-deploy was asked directly whether this derives I6 shipped-incomplete and answered no, with reasoning the orchestrator accepts: both the overlay header at :79-84 and docs/uat-environment.md state the gap plainly, and the readiness doc leaves the design question open in WS-D - specifically whether full-uat needs its own overlay file or should share this one via a second -f layer. Honest disclosure of a scoped gap is I8, not I6 false assurance, because nothing is advertised as covering full-uat. FIX: none required to ship; close the WS-D design question before the next observability PR rather than letting a second half-covered rig accumulate.
classification_rationale: a deliberate scope limit, disclosed in three places; recorded so the open design question is not lost

trigger: An operator mid-recovery follows auth-db-recovery.md's Related pointer to the corrected DR procedure on po/dr-procedure, which has no remote.
summary: A RECOVERY RUNBOOK DE-CERTIFIES THE DR PROCEDURE IN ITS OWN CHECKOUT AND POINTS AT A BRANCH THAT DOES NOT EXIST REMOTELY. The Related section tells the operator that 'this file's own copy is the pre-fix version' and to 'run the corrected procedure from that branch'. sre's operational judgement, which is the part Gate 2's version of this finding did not supply: the origin/dev DR procedure STILL WORKS - the defect it carries is the missing permission discipline, not an inability to restore - so the recovery path is degraded-but-usable rather than broken, and the dangling pointer fails VISIBLY when the operator cannot check the branch out. Visible, diagnosable failure is I8, not I4, and sre derived it that way explicitly. This overlaps sec5-5, doc5-F5 and doc5-F6 on the same underlying fact (assurance and runbook docs citing a local-only branch) but in a DIFFERENT FILE, so it is recorded separately and flagged for Gate 7 to merge into one fix rather than four. FIX: cite the tracking issue or PR number rather than a branch name, and state plainly that the checkout's DR procedure does restore, with the known permission defect called out inline so the operator can compensate manually.
classification_rationale: the runbook routes to an unreachable target; the operational consequence was assessed rather than assumed

trigger: A reader follows slo.md's describe-site citation for yuzu_fleet_agents_healthy to server.cpp:498, which describes only the sibling gauge.
summary: ONE CITATION SLIP IN AN OTHERWISE CLEAN PARITY SWEEP. slo.md:122-124 writes '(both gauges ... :2237 respectively; described server.cpp:498)'. sre verified that server.cpp:498 describes only yuzu_agents_connected; yuzu_fleet_agents_healthy is described at server.cpp:1926. Recorded at INFO and deliberately not inflated: the metric names are right, the emitting sites are right, the alert expressions are right, and only one of two describe-site pointers in a parenthetical is wrong. It is recorded at all because this change's whole thesis is citation accuracy in assurance documents, and because the surrounding sweep of seventeen other cited line numbers came back exact - which is what makes this one worth a one-line correction rather than a shrug. FIX: 'described server.cpp:498 and :1926 respectively'.
classification_rationale: the cited line does not hold the claimed symbol; verified at this sha

trigger: A reader encounters slo.md:132's paging language 50 lines before the same document corrects fires-versus-pages.
summary: THE COSMETIC RESIDUAL OF sre3-1, RECORDED SO THE CLOSURE IS HONEST RATHER THAN TIDY. slo.md:132 still reads 'so it never falsely pages'. The same document establishes at :180-190 that alerts FIRE and do not PAGE, because no Alertmanager ships. sre found this while sweeping the full claim surface to decide whether sre3-1 could close, and judged - correctly - that it does not reopen the blocker: the sentence is about false-positive suppression rather than a claim that a human is notified, and the document's substantive correction is present, complete and 50 lines later. Recording it separately keeps the sre3-1 closure clean: the blocker is fixed, one word is not, and both facts are in the ledger. FIX: 'so it never fires falsely'.
classification_rationale: residual paging language the same document corrects elsewhere; no claim is false in substance

trigger: n/a - Gate 3 clean-result record
summary: WHAT GATE 3 CHECKED BY EXECUTION AND CLEARED. (1) COMPOSE COMMAND-REPLACEMENT DROPS NOTHING: release-deploy verified the base UAT prometheus service has NO `command:` key, that the image default CMD is exactly --config.file=/etc/prometheus/prometheus.yml plus --storage.tsdb.path=/prometheus, and that the overlay's three-flag list is a strict SUPERSET - so no retention, --web.external-url or --web.console.* flag is silently lost. `volumes:` merged by container-path as expected and prometheus-uat-data:/prometheus survives in BOTH -f orders. This was a specific worry raised in the Gate 3 brief and it is answered. (2) THE DELETED deploy/grafana/yuzu-alerts.yml CAUSES NO BOOT FAILURE: no compose mount, no Grafana provisioning reference (deploy/grafana/provisioning/{dashboards,datasources}/*.yml do not name it), no packaging manifest. Its only two live consumers, scripts/docker-start-UAT.sh:148 and scripts/win-start-UAT.sh:194, are BOTH guarded by `if [ -f ... ]`, so the deletion degrades to a silent no-op rather than a startup error. architect separately confirmed zero remaining references anywhere in the tree. (3) PRODUCTION BLAST RADIUS IS NIL: docker-compose.reference.yml contains zero prometheus and zero grafana matches, so the overlay is inert in production exactly as the header and uat-environment.md both claim. (4) NO RELEASE-GATE INTERACTION beyond R5-3: the overlay defines no healthcheck and no image, so scripts/ci/verify-healthcheck-invariants.sh is not engaged. (5) CAPACITY IS A NON-QUESTION: sre confirmed the overlay adds no scrape targets - prometheus-observability.yml is prometheus-uat.yml's two jobs plus rule_files: - and evaluating 116 rules on a 10s interval against two targets is negligible; no new caches, buffers, queues or pools. (6) /readyz HAS NO PATTERN-E GAP: nothing in this change is newly load-bearing, and sre read the conjunction at server.cpp:13681+ to confirm it. (7) CAPABILITY-MAP AND ROADMAP ARE COHERENT: architect grepped both and found no mention of the overlay, yuzu-alerts, docs/assurance/ or slo.md, and ruled per arch5-1 that since the overlay is not a capability, NEITHER FILE SHOULD ACCRUE AN ENTRY - an explicit no-action ruling rather than an oversight.
classification_rationale: clean-result record across all three Gate 3 reviewers; closes the ledger's inability to distinguish a passing reviewer from an absent one

trigger: An operator applies the overlay, verifies 116 rules, then later restarts the rig with any base-only compose command - including scripts/win-start-UAT.sh:285, which docker-compose.uat.yml's own header advertises as the managed path.
summary: THE OVERLAY IS NOT STICKY, THE REPO'S OWN LAUNCHER SILENTLY STRIPS IT, AND THE RESULT IS INDISTINGUISHABLE FROM THE FAILURE THE CHANGE WAS WRITTEN TO PREVENT. THIS IS THE STRONGEST FINDING OF PASS 5: TWO AGENTS IN THE SAME GATE 4 WAVE REACHED IT INDEPENDENTLY AND BOTH EXECUTED IT - unhappy-path as UP5-7 and happy-path as HP5-1, neither able to see the other. Mechanism: the overlay only applies to the compose invocation that names it. scripts/win-start-UAT.sh:285 runs `docker compose -f docker-compose.uat.yml up -d` - base only - and docker-compose.uat.yml's own header advertises that script as the managed path. happy-path EXECUTED the sequence in an isolated project: after a green 116-rule overlay boot, a base-only `up -d` RECREATED the prometheus container, left it `Up` with both scrape jobs configured, and rules went to ZERO. The orchestrator independently confirmed the base-only invocation at win-start-UAT.sh:285. WHY THIS IS SEVERE RATHER THAN MERELY AWKWARD: the resulting state is byte-for-byte the observable state the overlay header itself calls BLOCKING for the reversed -f order - healthy container, every scrape target up, zero of 116 rules evaluated - except it is reached with NO operator mistake at all, by following the rig's own documented lifecycle. The operator additionally holds a prior successful verification transcript, so the evidence artefact says monitoring works while it does not. It compounds R5-1: the `promtool check config` alternative also exits 0 in this state. WHAT IS MISSING, per happy-path: any statement that every later compose command must repeat BOTH -f files; any warning that win-start-UAT.sh drops the overlay; and any teardown or return-to-plain-rig instruction at all. FIX: state the repeat-both-files rule at the top of the overlay header and in docs/uat-environment.md; add a warning to win-start-UAT.sh or teach it the overlay; document teardown.
classification_rationale: the persistence contract and the launcher interaction are both undocumented; the failure state was reproduced by execution by two independent agents

trigger: Re-running the rig's own documented launcher (scripts/win-start-UAT.sh) or the base compose file's own usage line after a successful overlay boot.
summary: SAME DEFECT AS UP5-7, RAISED INDEPENDENTLY BY THE OTHER GATE 4 AGENT AND RECORDED AS ITS OWN ROW SO THE CONVERGENCE IS COUNTABLE. happy-path reached it from the opposite direction - walking the CORRECT path end to end rather than hunting failures - which is why it also establishes what WORKS. Executed in an isolated compose project (-p hp5probe, port 19090, torn down with `down -v`; the operator's live docker project was never touched): the documented cold start from `cd deploy/docker` with the documented -f order yields 116 rules across 21 groups, ALL with health=ok and lastEvaluation set. Idempotency PASSES - `up -d` twice leaves it Running, `POST /-/reload` twice returns 200 then 200, and the verification command is read-only. So the happy path itself is sound and that is recorded as a clean result. THEN the defect: a base-only `up -d` recreated the container and rules went to 0. happy-path derived I6 raised to HIGH via the false-assurance clause, on the reasoning that a verified-green count plus a healthy stack plus zero rules IS a control advertised as in force that is not - and the orchestrator accepts that derivation. NATIVE-VS-DERIVED DISAGREEMENT, REPORTED AS REQUIRED: happy-path labelled this SHOULD; its own stated facts derive HIGH and the derived band governs the gate. FIX: as UP5-7 - the two are one fix.
classification_rationale: independent confirmation of UP5-7 from the normal-path direction; also records that the documented happy path and its idempotency otherwise pass

trigger: An operator or auditor computes an error budget or availability figure over a [30d] window on the UAT or observability stack, where Prometheus runs with its default 15-day retention.
summary: EVERY SLO IN THE DOCUMENT IS DENOMINATED OVER 30 DAYS AND NO SHIPPED PROMETHEUS CAN HOLD 30 DAYS OF DATA. All five SLOs in slo.md specify 30-day rolling windows. No shipped Prometheus config sets --storage.tsdb.retention.time anywhere, leaving Prometheus's 15-day default. unhappy-path verified this by grep and the orchestrator independently re-ran it: `grep -rn 'storage.tsdb' deploy/` returns EXACTLY ONE hit, `--storage.tsdb.path=/prometheus` at docker-compose.observability.yml:101. No document in the change mentions retention at all. WHY THIS DERIVES I3 RATHER THAN A MERE GAP: `avg_over_time(...[30d])` does not error and does not warn when the data does not span 30 days - it silently evaluates over whatever exists, roughly 15 days, and returns a number that is indistinguishable in form from a true 30-day figure. A reported '99.7% over 30d' is a 15-day figure wearing a 30-day label, and the caller cannot tell. That is the definition of I3. This lands squarely on this change's own thesis: the document's central promise is that its numbers are measured and honest, and the measurement window it specifies cannot be satisfied by the stack it ships. NOTE ON SCOPE: this is NOT a finding that an SLO TARGET is wrong, which would be a PO decision and out of bounds - it is a finding that the target as specified is not computable from anything that ships, which the brief explicitly admits. FIX: set --storage.tsdb.retention.time=31d (or longer) in the overlay, or state in slo.md that 30-day figures require a retention change the UAT rig does not make.
classification_rationale: the stated measurement window contradicts the shipped retention; verified by grep across deploy/

trigger: An audit-store incident with intermittent emit failures; an incident reviewer or SOC-2 assessor reads slo.md section 4 and concludes that because the counter was non-zero, all behavioural-PII reads were withheld for the duration.
summary: THE AUDIT SLO DESCRIBES A GLOBAL-COUNTER-TO-ROUTE-BEHAVIOUR COUPLING THAT DOES NOT EXIST, AND IT PRODUCES A FALSE SOC-2 EVIDENCE STATEMENT. slo.md states that the named behavioural-PII REST routes return 503 and withhold data 'THE MOMENT yuzu_server_audit_emit_failed_total rises'. The orchestrator confirmed that wording verbatim at :174-176. The actual mechanism is PER-REQUEST: server/core/src/rest_audit.hpp:130-152 fails closed on the request whose OWN audit emit failed. A failed emit on request A does not withhold request B. The counter is a fleet-wide aggregate; the control is request-scoped. They are not the same claim. CONSEQUENCE, which is why this derives I1 alongside I3: the natural reading produces a written incident or compliance statement of the form 'no behavioural-PII was served unaudited during the window', and the code does not support it - requests whose own emit succeeded were served normally throughout, and nothing correlates an individual request to the aggregate counter. Under this project's standing position that SOC-2 evidence-integrity gaps are a firm HIGH and are not to be soft-pedalled, an assurance document that licenses a false evidence statement about an audit control is exactly the case that rule exists for. AGGRAVATING FACTOR unhappy-path identified: the SAME BRANCH's shared-responsibility-matrix.md row 35 states the carve-out CORRECTLY - 'dashboard HTML + MCP are set-and-proceed on a write failure' - so two assurance artefacts shipped in one commit disagree about the same control, and slo.md is the one the readiness doc's WS-D cites as the SLO evidence. FIX: restate as per-request fail-closed, name the set-and-proceed surfaces explicitly as the matrix already does, and remove 'the moment ... rises'.
classification_rationale: the document's stated control semantics contradict rest_audit.hpp and contradict its own sibling matrix row

trigger: Any auth or Postgres-unreachable incident - the runbook's own subject - in which the operator runs the build-discriminator query; the connection fails, which the doc's decision rule cannot distinguish from a missing relation.
summary: THE DISCRIMINATOR IS UNREACHABLE DURING THE EXACT INCIDENT THE RUNBOOK COVERS, AND ITS FAILURE BRANCH IS THE DANGEROUS ONE. THIS IS A DISTINCT DEFECT FROM sec5-1 AND A NAME FIX WILL NOT REPAIR IT. sec5-1 owns the fact that `session_store.schema_meta` is the wrong relation. unhappy-path owns the deeper problem: the discriminator is a POSTGRES QUERY, and it is invoked in a runbook whose own subject includes the section 'Postgres unreachable'. So during a Postgres outage the query fails from CONNECTION REFUSAL, not from a missing relation - and the doc's rule reads ANY failure as 'you are on the legacy build and restart DOES help'. A connection failure and a relation-missing failure are not distinguished anywhere in the text. SYMPTOM: on a durable-session build the operator restarts the server, believes the compromised session is dead, and the session rehydrates from session_store.sessions when Postgres returns. No error, no log line, and no metric distinguishes 'revoked' from 'restarted and repopulated'. The restart also inflicts the outage the same document elsewhere warns against. EXPOSURE is E2 and that is load-bearing: an attacker holding a stolen session retains privilege past the operator's containment step, so the actor ends up beyond the privilege the operator believed they had removed. E2 would raise the band, and I4's cap holds it at HIGH. TOGETHER WITH sec5-1 AND UP5-3 this is three independent defects in one decision mechanism, all resolving to the same wrong branch, in a procedure executed under active compromise. FIX: use a discriminator that does not depend on the degraded component, and distinguish connection failure from relation-absent explicitly - the doc must tell the operator what to do when it cannot tell.
classification_rationale: the decision rule's failure branch is stated as diagnostic when it cannot distinguish two causes with opposite correct actions

trigger: A session compromise concurrent with a Postgres outage on a SessionStore (durable-session) build.
summary: ON A DURABLE-SESSION BUILD DURING A POSTGRES OUTAGE NO DOCUMENTED REVOCATION PATH WORKS, AND THE RUNBOOK ASSERTS THAT ONE DOES. The runbook states the REST revocation surface 'is the only thing that actually revokes a session on this build'. unhappy-path traced it: AuthManager::wipe_user_sessions_durable (server/core/src/auth.cpp:572-582) returns false on store failure - which is CORRECT, fail-closed behaviour and the right design - so DELETE /api/v1/sessions?username=... errors while the store is degraded. Restart is ruled out by the same section. The runbook then offers no third option. The software is behaving properly; the DOCUMENT is the defect, because it advertises a containment capability as available without disclosing that it is unreachable in the compound state most likely to accompany a compromise. That is I6 raised to HIGH under the false-assurance clause, not a software bug. OBSERVED CONSEQUENCE unhappy-path drew out: the operator receives a non-2xx from the only documented revocation call, has exhausted the runbook, and improvises - and the most probable improvisation is the restart that UP5-1 shows is both ineffective and believed effective. The two findings chain. NATIVE-VS-DERIVED DISAGREEMENT, REPORTED AS REQUIRED: unhappy-path labelled SHOULD on the explicit ground that the software behaves correctly, then noted that I6-with-false-assurance plus the absent fallback derives HIGH and that the derived band governs. The orchestrator endorses that self-correction - it is exactly the discipline the severity rule asks for. FIX: document what to do when the store is degraded, even if the honest answer is 'containment is not available until Postgres returns; isolate at the network layer'.
classification_rationale: the fallback for the compound state is absent while the capability is asserted as available

trigger: An operator on an untagged, intermediate, or fork build falls through to the --version fallback after the SQL discriminator fails.
summary: THE FALLBACK DISCRIMINATOR NAMES NO BOUNDARY AND CANNOT EXPRESS ONE, SO BOTH BRANCHES ARE GUESSES. The runbook offers, as its second discriminator, 'the binary's own --version predating this fix'. It names NO VERSION NUMBER. This project's standing convention is that meson versions are always plain X.Y.Z with no -dev or -rcN suffix, so a dev build carrying SessionStore is indistinguishable by --version from a tagged build without it. An operator reading `0.13.1` cannot map that to either side of the HA-WS-1 boundary. Both available guesses are actionable and one of them is wrong in a way that leaves a compromised session live. This is the THIRD independent defect in the same decision mechanism, after sec5-1 (wrong relation) and UP5-1 (cannot distinguish connection failure from relation-absent) - and it matters most precisely because it is the fallback the other two failures route the operator into. A fallback that cannot answer is worse than no fallback, because it terminates the operator's search for a real answer. unhappy-path named a working alternative that already exists and is unused: `SELECT 1 FROM session_store.sessions LIMIT 1`, or the presence of the yuzu_auth_session_store_degrade_total series. NATIVE-VS-DERIVED DISAGREEMENT: labelled SHOULD, derives HIGH on I4 (a named action whose selection mechanism cannot produce a correct answer), capped at HIGH. Derived governs. FIX: name the actual version boundary, and replace the SQL probe with one that works.
classification_rationale: the version boundary the fallback depends on is absent from the document and unexpressible in the project's version scheme

trigger: Any deployment with auditing disabled or the audit sink unconfigured; the SLO reports 100% attainment and its alert never fires because the counter never rises.
summary: THE AUDIT-WRITE SLO IS TRIVIALLY GREEN ON AN AUDIT-DISABLED DEPLOYMENT, WHICH IS THE ONE STATE IT MOST NEEDS TO CATCH. Section 4's target is '0 emit failures / 30d' and its alert is `increase(yuzu_server_audit_emit_failed_total[5m]) > 0`. unhappy-path traced rest_audit.hpp:80,117: when audit is off the helper returns true and serves, so no emit is attempted and the failure counter never rises. Result: a perfectly-met audit-write SLO, no firing alert, and zero audit records - a control reported at 100% attainment while entirely absent. That is I6 under the false-assurance clause, and I3 because the reported figure is wrong and the reader cannot tell. WHAT MAKES THIS ACTIONABLE RATHER THAN THEORETICAL, and unhappy-path found it: the canonical rules file ALREADY SHIPS the correct pattern for exactly this problem - yuzu-alerts.yml:2341 is YuzuAuditRetentionMetricMissing, an absent()-shaped liveness pair. So the fix is not an invention, it is applying a pattern this repo already uses one file away, to the SLO that most needs it. E4 is recorded because audit-disabled is non-default, and E4 is explicitly NOT a downgrade in this codebase - the project's own severity rule notes that the default is frequently the less hardened setting, and an audit-disabled deployment is precisely a deployment whose operator has already chosen less assurance. NATIVE-VS-DERIVED DISAGREEMENT: labelled SHOULD, derives HIGH. Derived governs. FIX: add an absent()-based liveness SLI for the audit path alongside the failure-count SLI, modelled on the existing rule.
classification_rationale: a liveness SLI for the audit path is absent, so the failure-count SLI reads green in the absent case

trigger: The documented verification is run once at overlay bring-up; afterwards any of a base-only restart (UP5-7), a rejected reload (sec5-3), a stray .yml crash-loop (R5-2), or an unauthenticated POST /-/quit (sec5-2) returns the stack to zero or stale rules.
summary: THE DOCUMENTED VERIFICATION IS A POINT-IN-TIME COUNT WITH NO EXPIRY, NO TIMESTAMP, AND NO RE-RUN CONTRACT, AND THREE DOCUMENTS PRESENT IT AS THE EVIDENCE THAT RULES ARE LIVE. This is the synthesis finding of the unhappy-path register and it names the shape the whole change keeps reproducing. `curl /api/v1/rules | assert n >= 115` proves something was true once. Nothing records when, nothing says how often to repeat it, and four separate ordinary events afterwards return the stack to a zero-or-stale state while the transcript stays green. The sec5-3 variant is the nastiest: on a REJECTED reload Prometheus keeps the previously-loaded set, so the count still reads 116 and the assertion still passes while the rules being evaluated are the PREVIOUS ones - an operator who edited a threshold believes the new threshold is live when it is not. unhappy-path also identified a compounding mechanism the orchestrator had not considered: under `restart: unless-stopped`, a repeated unauthenticated POST /-/quit resets `for:` timers on every restart, so an alert with `for: 5m` can be prevented from EVER reaching firing state while the container never appears unhealthy and /api/v1/rules keeps returning 116 between kills. EXPOSURE is recorded as E0 for the finding as scored - no actor is required for the restart and reload variants. unhappy-path explicitly DECLINED to re-adjudicate the E1 raise for the /-/quit variant, noting sec5-2 already owns that exposure at MEDIUM and recording it here only as an amplifier; that restraint is correct and is recorded. FIX: make the verification content-sensitive (assert a named rule present and its health=ok, not a count), stamp it with a timestamp, and state a re-run contract - after every compose command, not once.
classification_rationale: the verification's validity window and re-run contract are absent; the states that invalidate it were each established by execution at Gates 3 and 4

trigger: A customer security reviewer or SOC-2 assessor with clone access to origin only follows a citation in docs/assurance/ to po/dr-procedure, or tries to determine the current value of the CA-custody row.
summary: A MATRIX ROW'S RATING VALUE IS MADE CONDITIONAL ON EVIDENCE NO EXTERNAL READER CAN REACH, WHICH IS DIFFERENT IN KIND FROM AN UNRESOLVABLE SOURCE CITATION - AND THIS ROW CARRIES A GENUINE THREE-WAY BAND DISAGREEMENT THAT THE OPERATOR SHOULD ADJUDICATE. The fact is agreed by everyone: docs/assurance/** cites po/dr-procedure and two filenames that exist on no reachable ref, and security-guardian verified `origin/po/dr-procedure` does not exist. THE DISAGREEMENT IS ABOUT WHAT IT COSTS. security-guardian derived LOW (sec5-5) on the ground that no CONTROL is claimed in force, every citation is paired with an explicit not-shipped label, and the underlying disclosures are true - so it is evidence-traceability, not false assurance. consistency-auditor independently swept all 8 citations and found the LABELLING CLEAN. unhappy-path derives HIGH on a narrower and different point: matrix:20 does not merely cite the branch, it makes the ROW'S RATING conditional on it - 'treat this row as the full-responsibility mark only once that fix has actually landed in the procedure you run' - so a reader cannot determine the row's CURRENT VALUE at all without tracking an unmerged branch they cannot fetch. happy-path reached the same point independently as HP5-7, calling the cell 'unanswerable without tracking an unmerged branch', which is why independent_reporters is 2 for this specific claim rather than 1. unhappy-path also argued the failure is global rather than local for an assurance artefact: a runbook with a dangling citation fails one step, but an artefact whose entire authority is 'every claim cites its source' invites the reviewer to discount every claim they cannot independently verify, including the true ones. NATIVE-VS-DERIVED DISAGREEMENT: unhappy-path labelled SHOULD, noting the branch split is a PO decision, then derived HIGH and observed - correctly - that the PO ruling makes the SPLIT out of scope but does not make a dangling citation in a customer-facing artefact out of scope. RECORDED AT THE DERIVED HIGH WITHOUT RE-ADJUDICATION, with the dissent preserved; the orchestrator flags this as the one band on this pass most worth an operator ruling. FIX: give the row a determinate current value (it is shared responsibility today) and cite an issue or PR number rather than a branch.
classification_rationale: the row's stated value is indeterminate to its intended reader; the underlying unreachability is verified and the band is disputed across three agents, recorded rather than resolved

trigger: A prospective customer performs due diligence against the whitepaper, then deploys v0.13.0 - the only tagged release - in which six of the enumerated control families do not exist.
summary: THE WHITEPAPER ANCHORS ITS ENTIRE POSTURE TO A COMMIT NO CUSTOMER CAN OBTAIN, AND ITS SHIPPED CONTROLS ARE ABSENT FROM THE ONLY INSTALLABLE ARTEFACT. The document anchors to `dev @ d295db964` and then enumerates six control families - the PostgreSQL audit store, CaStore, RbacStore, ManagementGroupStore, SessionStore, and MCP Streamable HTTP - none of which exist in v0.13.0, the only tagged release. unhappy-path was careful to record what the document does WELL, and the orchestrator preserves it: the disclosure block is explicit, prominent and per-control, which is far better than the alternative and is why this is I6 rather than outright deception. The residual is that the reader is left with no obtainable build in which the document's posture holds, and NO WORKING PROCEDURE for determining which controls a given build has. THE INVERSION THAT MAKES THIS LOAD-BEARING RATHER THAN PEDANTIC: the whitepaper states that v0.13.0 sessions are in-memory and do not survive a restart, which is the exact OPPOSITE of the dev-HEAD guidance in auth-db-recovery.md - so the one place a reader most needs a reliable build check is the place where the two documents give opposite instructions, and the only mechanism offered to tell them apart is the discriminator that sec5-1, UP5-1 and UP5-3 have now shown to be broken three separate ways. A security review can therefore approve a posture the deployed artefact does not have, with no documented way to notice. NATIVE-VS-DERIVED DISAGREEMENT: labelled SHOULD, derives HIGH on I6 false-assurance plus I3. Derived governs. FIX: state the posture per RELEASE rather than per commit, or ship a working build-capability probe the document can point at.
classification_rationale: controls documented as shipped are absent from the only obtainable artefact, and the offered means of telling which build one is on does not work

trigger: An operator on macOS or Linux follows the new docs/uat-environment.md section; scripts/start-UAT.sh never starts docker-compose.uat.yml, so the Prometheus stack must be hand-started and the document does not say so.
summary: THE OVERLAY'S PREREQUISITE IS NEVER STATED, AND ON THE CANONICAL LINUX/MACOS RIG THE PREREQUISITE IS NOT EVEN SATISFIED BY THE DOCUMENTED LAUNCHER. happy-path executed the missing-prerequisite case: with no native server running, the overlay comes up perfectly clean, the yuzu-server scrape target is DOWN, and 116 rules evaluate forever against empty data - while the documented verification still reports '116'. So the change's own success criterion is met in a state where the monitoring observes nothing at all. COMPOUNDING FACT happy-path established by reading the scripts: scripts/start-UAT.sh, which docs/uat-environment.md:11 presents as the canonical Linux/macOS rig, NEVER starts docker-compose.uat.yml - it brings up only a `docker run` postgres sidecar. The only launcher that starts this compose file is the Windows script. So on macOS and Linux the entire Prometheus stack must be hand-started, and the new section never mentions it. MISSING STEP, which is the class happy-path exists to find: 'start the rig first', plus a statement of what the overlay expects to be running. FIX: state the prerequisite explicitly and add a scrape-target check (assert the yuzu-server target is up) alongside the rule count, so the verification observes reachability and not only parse success.
classification_rationale: a required prerequisite step is missing from a documented operator workflow

trigger: An operator whose goal is confidence that alerting works follows the documented path, which ends at '116 rules are loaded'.
summary: THE HAPPY PATH STOPS ONE STEP SHORT OF ITS OWN PURPOSE, AND THE MISSING STEP IS FREE. Loaded is not firing, and the change's stated claim is that the rules are 'evaluated by a live system'. happy-path executed the missing step to prove it is available: on a bare boot, three rules go to `pending` and `GET /api/v1/alerts` returns THREE ALERTS - YuzuAuditRetentionMetricMissing, YuzuInstructionBundledContentNotClean and YuzuResponseReapMetricMissing. So firing IS observable, immediately, at an endpoint that NEITHER new document names as a step; slo.md mentions /api/v1/alerts only in passing prose. The shipped one-liner counts rules rather than asserting health=ok or lastEvaluation, so what it actually proves is parse-and-load, not evaluation - which is a weaker claim than the one the change makes. This is the constructive counterpart to UP5-8: the verification can be made content-sensitive and evaluation-sensitive using data the stack already exposes, at no cost. MISSING STEP: an /api/v1/alerts check with its expected shape. FIX: add the alerts query to the documented path and assert health=ok and a non-empty lastEvaluation on the rule groups, not merely a count.
classification_rationale: the step that would substantiate the change's own central claim is missing, and was shown to be available at no cost

trigger: An operator attempts to compute SLO attainment, or to respond to a breach, using only slo.md.
summary: EVERY SLO IS MISSING TWO OF THE SIX LINKS IN ITS OWN CHAIN: THE SLI EXPRESSION AND THE BREACH RESPONSE. happy-path traced metric -> SLI -> target -> window -> alert -> response for all five SLOs. (a) NO SLI EXPRESSION EXISTS for any of the five. '99.5% over 30d' and 'p99 under 10s for at least 99% of 5-minute windows' have no PromQL that computes attainment, so the PO-mandated 90-day re-baseline has no method at all - and section 3's clamp_min note is prose guidance, not an expression. (b) NO BREACH RESPONSE for four of the five: only section 4 carries a Runbook: line, while sections 1, 2, 3 and 5a-c name an alert and stop, and docs/ops-runbooks/ contains no runbook for any of them. An SLO with a target and no documented response is incomplete on the SUCCESS path, which is precisely the class this reviewer is charged with and which the failure-hunting agents do not look for. unhappy-path independently reached the (a) half from the opposite direction as UP5-14, observing that section 3's target is not computable from anything that ships and that an operator who substitutes the shipped alert's raw expression reproduces the negative-offset error section 3 itself warns about - so independent_reporters is 2 for the missing-SLI half. NOTE ON SCOPE: this is not a comment on the TARGET NUMBERS, which are PO decisions and out of bounds; it is that the document does not supply the means to evaluate or act on them. FIX: add one PromQL SLI per SLO and either a Runbook: line or an explicit 'no runbook yet' per section.
classification_rationale: two required links of each SLO's own stated chain are absent; confirmed independently from both the success and failure directions

trigger: An operator follows auth-db-recovery.md's new backup section, then needs to restore; the cited DR page's restore path does not cover the database or the keys directory, and the runbook tells them not to rely on that page anyway.
summary: THE RUNBOOK SHIPS A BACKUP PROCEDURE WITH NO REACHABLE RESTORE, AND THE REAL RESTORE EXISTS BUT IS NOT CITED. The new 'Backup - the KEK pairing rule' section documents `pg_dump --format=custom` plus a `tar` of the certs directory, and a later 'Post-restore verification' section assumes a restore has happened. So the documented backup has no documented restore. happy-path found that the REAL procedure does exist, at docs/user-manual/server-admin.md:2776-2788, and is simply UNCITED here - which makes this a cheap fix rather than missing work. ALSO MISSING, and it is the exact drift the KEK section itself predicts: restoring the extracted certs archive says nothing about ownership or file mode, so a restore can silently widen permissions on the key material the section exists to protect. NOTE ON SCOPE: this is NOT a DR-procedure defect raised against the stacked branch - scripts/yuzu-restore.sh is byte-identical to origin/dev here and its own limitations are pre-existing and out of scope. The finding is that THIS branch's new backup section, which is in scope, points at a restore path that cannot complete it. FIX: cite server-admin.md:2776-2788 as the restore counterpart, and state the ownership/mode restoration step for the certs archive.
classification_rationale: the restore counterpart to a newly documented backup is absent from the runbook although it exists elsewhere in the tree

trigger: An operator runs the runbook's post-restore verification on a server that came back DEGRADED rather than healthy.
summary: THE POST-RESTORE VERIFICATION DOES NOT ESTABLISH SUCCESS - A DIRECT AND WELL-EVIDENCED CHALLENGE TO sre's GATE 3 ASSESSMENT, RECORDED AS A GENUINE SECOND OPINION. sre judged the verification story sound, citing four steps. happy-path examined the same four and found each insufficient: STEP 1's only HTTP check is /health, whose handler sets no res.status and returns 200 with a body of 'status':'degraded' (server.cpp around :13560 and :13673) - so it PASSES on a degraded server; the surrounding comment even names /readyz (:13681, the conjunctive store check) but no command in the step actually uses it. STEP 2 prints schema_meta.version with NO EXPECTED VALUE, so there is no pass/fail criterion. STEP 3 pipes to `grep secret_decrypt_failures_total`, which EXITS 1 on the documented-correct outcome, since the doc says the series is absent entirely when all is well - the success case looks like a failed command. STEP 4 - 'a real MFA login works end-to-end', which the document itself calls the decisive check - is a bare comment with no procedure at all. TWO AGENTS, TWO CONCLUSIONS, ON THE SAME TEXT: the orchestrator records both without re-adjudicating. happy-path's is the more specific and is supported by handler-level evidence; sre's was a higher-level judgement that the steps exist and are ordered. Derived LOW because a restore that is verified weakly still usually succeeds and the failure is visible when it does not. FIX: use /readyz not /health; state the expected schema version; invert step 3's check; write step 4 out as a procedure.
classification_rationale: the verification steps do not test what they are presented as testing; established against the request handlers

trigger: An auditor reads the readiness doc's section 3.4 and treats the stale-inode fix as empirically verified.

NATIVE-VS-DERIVED DISAGREEMENT: labelled SHOULD, derives LOW because I8 caps there. Derived governs, and the orchestrator notes the derivation is correct - nothing operational goes wrong, the cost is credibility in an audit. trigger: Gate 7 aggregates findings by policy_floor; R5-1 is the same false-green class as sec5-1/doc5-F1 but carries policy_floor null.
summary: THE AUDITOR AUDITED THE EVIDENCE RECORD ITSELF AND CAUGHT AN INCONSISTENT FLOOR ATTRIBUTION BY THE ORCHESTRATOR. sec5-1 and doc5-F1 carry policy_floor set to the false-green clause. R5-1 is the identical class - a promtool check config 'verification' that exits 0 against the broken mount set, offered two lines below the R4-1 fix as its alternative closure - yet the orchestrator recorded policy_floor null on it. The orchestrator ACCEPTS this: the row recorded release-deploy's own judgement that the floor was 'applicable-but-arguable' because the PRIMARY check is sound, and rested the gate on the derived HIGH instead. That reasoning is defensible and is preserved, but the auditor is right that the resulting record is inconsistent across three rows of the same class, and a reader aggregating by policy_floor gets a different answer than a reader aggregating by derived band. EXPOSURE is E6 and that is why this is LOW rather than higher: R5-1's derived band is ALREADY HIGH and already blocking, so no verdict can change on this - the wrong outcome is proven unable to occur. This is recorded rather than silently corrected because the ledger's own rule is that a row is superseded, never edited, and because an orchestrator quietly amending its own floor attributions is exactly the shape the de-escalation guard exists to make visible. RESOLUTION: left to the operator; the gate is unaffected either way.
classification_rationale: inconsistent floor attribution across three rows of one class inside the evidence record this run produces

trigger: Reading ledger row R5-3, whose impact I9 and exposure E0 derive INFO while the row records derived_band LOW.
summary: A SECOND SELF-AUDIT CATCH: ONE LEDGER ROW'S BAND DOES NOT FOLLOW FROM ITS OWN DERIVATION FIELDS. R5-3 records impact I9 and exposure E0, which derive INFO, but the row states derived_band LOW. The orchestrator independently re-ran the check and confirms the fields are I9 / E0 / LOW / NICE. consistency-auditor noted that the comparable rows - sre5-1, arch5-5, R5-2 and others - all derive correctly, so this is an isolated slip rather than a systematic mis-derivation. DELIBERATE NON-ACTION, AND THE REASONING IS RECORDED BECAUSE IT IS NOT OBVIOUS: the row is NOT being superseded to INFO. Under the stronger-of rule a finding is read at the stronger of its facts and its label, so R5-3 already reads at LOW and nothing is under-counted; whereas appending a row that moves the band DOWNWARD would be a de-escalation requiring an adjudicated_by attestation from someone who is not the author - a real cost, incurred to change a NICE finding to a slightly more NICE finding, on a row whose gate impact is nil either way. The honest record is the auditor's catch sitting next to the original row, which is what this produces. The wider value is that the ledger was audited as a component like any other and two defects in it were found by an agent other than its writer.
classification_rationale: a recorded band that does not follow from its own recorded facts; left in place under the stronger-of rule rather than de-escalated

trigger: A reader of whitepaper section 3.8 looks for rbac_enabled in server.hpp, which the column header says is the config source.

trigger: n/a - Gate 5 test-design record; nothing was executed
summary: GATE 5 RAN BECAUSE GATE 4 PRODUCED FINDINGS, AND IT PRODUCED A TEST DESIGN, NOT NEW FINDINGS. Eight scenarios, all designed against an isolated compose project (-p ch5probe) on port 19090 so nothing touches the operator's live docker project, and all excluding DR-procedure chaos, which lives on po/dr-procedure. TWO FLAGSHIP COMPOUNDS. CH5-1, THE MONITORING VOID BEHIND GREEN EVIDENCE, chains FIVE findings in four legs against one rig using ONLY documented commands: L1 runs the exact win-start-UAT.sh:285 base-only invocation after a green 116-rule boot (UP5-7); L2 posts a reload with an invalid scratch rules file and re-runs the documented count (sec5-3); L3 runs the header's own promtool check config alternative in both broken states (R5-1); L4 loops an unauthenticated POST /-/quit every 120s for 20 minutes against restart: unless-stopped while a for: 5m condition is held true (sec5-2 + UP5-8). Its deliverable is the right one: a SINGLE TRANSCRIPT interleaving each green verification line with the concurrent /api/v1/rules and /api/v1/alerts ground truth - the operator holding green evidence over a dead monitoring plane. The hypothesis is stated falsifiably and each leg carries its expected FAIL, so the run has a defined outcome rather than an exploration. CH5-2, THE REVOCATION-DECISION BRANCH MEASUREMENT, is procedural rather than technical and is the more original design: give five or more readers a scripted active-compromise scenario with a ten-minute box, on a mix of durable-session dev-HEAD and v0.13.0 rigs, with POSTGRES STOPPED on half the durable rigs so the discriminator fails with a CONNECTION error rather than relation-does-not-exist, and record keystrokes and stated conclusions. It measures which branch a reader ACTUALLY takes rather than which branch the text implies, which is the only way to size sec5-1, UP5-1, UP5-2 and UP5-3 as the single mechanism they are. Its success criteria include the honest reflexive case: if any reader's discriminator query SUCCEEDS, that falsifies the design's assumption rather than the finding. SIX FURTHER SCENARIOS: CH5-3 backfills 40 days of synthetic samples via promtool tsdb create-blocks-from and runs all five SLO expressions verbatim to expose the silent 15-day answer (UP5-4); CH5-4 stops Postgres mid-run with interleaved PII requests to test whether audit fail-closed is per-request or global, then boots audit-disabled to show SLO section 4 reading 100% with zero records, and simultaneously asserts up{job=yuzu-server} to catch UP5-16's ~100%-availability-during-degradation (UP5-5 + UP5-6 + UP5-16); CH5-5 drops a scratch .yml to trigger the crash-loop then tests the no--f reload (R5-2 + sec5-2 + sec5-3); CH5-6 boots the overlay with no fleet at all (HP5-2 + HP5-3); CH5-7 tests :ro edit-and-reload threshold loss and rule SUBSTITUTION against the count floor (UP5-9 + UP5-10); and CH5-8 needs no rig at all - it hands a reader with origin-only clone access three questions this branch cannot answer (UP5-11 + UP5-12 + UP5-13). Every scenario carries a rollback, and every one writes only to scratch copies, never to the tracked docs/prometheus/yuzu-alerts.yml, whose mount stays read-only.
classification_rationale: Gate 5 test-design record; chaos is a producer of test designs, not of findings

trigger: n/a - Gate 5 scope decision
summary: THE SCOPE DECISION, AND THE DISCIPLINE IN IT IS WORTH RECORDING AS MUCH AS THE CONTENT. chaos-injector was told that P0/P1/P2 is a scenario-planning label and NOT a gate, and that a scenario blocks only if its underlying finding derives CRITICAL/HIGH or hits a policy floor. It held that line explicitly and stated it in its own report: 'No new blocking status is created here.' FOUR SCENARIOS ARE P0, each because its UNDERLYING finding already derives HIGH independently: CH5-1 (UP5-7 and UP5-8 HIGH verified, plus R5-1 HIGH); CH5-2 (sec5-1 and doc5-F1 HIGH WITH a policy floor, plus UP5-1, UP5-2 and UP5-3 HIGH verified, I1 and I4 under active compromise); CH5-3 (UP5-4 HIGH verified at E0); CH5-4 (UP5-5 and UP5-6 HIGH verified, I3 on a SOC-2 evidence statement, which this project's standing position treats as a firm HIGH). THE MOST USEFUL SENTENCE IN THE WHOLE GATE 5 REPORT, and the orchestrator elevates it here because it is the correct reading of what a chaos design is FOR: these four need not be EXECUTED before push, because the findings already block on their own merits. What blocks is that the artefacts these scenarios would produce must not be CONTRADICTED by text shipping in this PR. That converts the chaos design from a pre-merge cost into a specification of what the fix has to make true - fix the doc claims (UP5-5, UP5-6, UP5-13), add the retention flag or drop the 30-day window (UP5-4), repair the discriminator and name a third revocation option (sec5-1, UP5-1, UP5-2, UP5-3), and make the overlay verification expiry-bearing (UP5-7, UP5-8). FILED AS FOLLOW-UPS, NON-BLOCKING, with the reasoning stated rather than assumed: CH5-5 (R5-2, sec5-2, sec5-3 at MEDIUM and LOW), CH5-6 (HP5-2, HP5-3 at MEDIUM), CH5-7 (UP5-9, UP5-10 at LOW), plus the SLO section 3 recording-rule and section 1 SLI gaps (UP5-14 and sre5-1 at MEDIUM) and UP5-15 at LOW - none derives HIGH, none hits a floor, and chaos-injector explicitly declined to manufacture blockers from them. CH5-8 is split correctly: the SCENARIO is P1, but UP5-11 and UP5-12 derive HIGH independently and are already blocking findings, so the chaos run would add evidence rather than gating. C5-1 through C5-4 generate NO scenarios at all, because they are ledger and label corrections rather than fault-injectable behaviour - a distinction chaos-injector drew itself and which is correct.

summary: THE CITATION CHAIN TURNS UP5-5 INTO A CORROBORATED FALSE CC7.2 EVIDENCE ARTEFACT - THIS IS THE COMPLIANCE CONSEQUENCE, NOT A RE-RAISE. compliance-officer traced the chain rather than assuming it: readiness section 3.4 at :299-305 ELEVATES slo.md to a WS-D deliverable evidence artefact, and security-whitepaper.md:274-276 cites slo.md section 4 as 'the write-success SLO built on this control'. trigger: Any external reader - customer security reviewer or SOC-2 assessor - follows a Source cell in docs/assurance/ to po/dr-procedure, which has no remote.

Sites: matrix:20, :25, :26; readiness:313-316; whitepaper:305-309; slo.md:278. CC8.1 is specific that evidence must be reviewable independently of its author, and a local-only branch is definitionally not. COMPOUNDED by customer-facing cells citing internal governance IDs - co3-2, UP4-12, sre6-5 and sre6-4 - as follow-up pointers at matrix:20, :25 and :32; none is externally resolvable and sre6-4 has no issue number at all. Both derivations are correct against their own criteria and are recorded without collapsing them. FIX, and compliance-officer noted it is a one-command discharge: push the branch and cite the PR URL, or mark the citations 'not yet published'; replace governance IDs with issue numbers.

THE ORCHESTRATOR ACCEPTS THIS AS THE GATE 6b WORK ITEM and notes it was independently arrived at: the operator's instruction for this pass already required split supersessions for the travelled findings, and compliance-officer reached the same requirement from the CC8.1 direction without being told. trigger: An assessor or operator asks which tracker covers the seven retired Grafana alerts; the readiness doc tables all seven but cites no issue number.
summary: THE RETIREMENT IS NARRATED EXCELLENTLY AND LINKED TO NOTHING. compliance-officer credited the WHAT - readiness:337-355 tables all seven lost alerts individually, which is better traceability of the content than most deletions get - and then found the gap: the string '#4231' appears NOWHERE in the diff, and the text says only 'propose these seven as new issues'. trigger: po/dr-procedure merges; every 'unmodified from origin/dev' and 'the fix is not yet merged' assertion in the customer-facing matrix becomes false on that day, with no mechanism to notice.

This is the compliance consequence of arch5-6 and an escalation of pass-1's co-6 rather than a duplicate of either, and compliance-officer identified what is NEW at pass 5: the matrix now carries assertions that are guaranteed to go false on a specific future event. 'Both unmodified from origin/dev', 'the fix is not yet merged', 'treat this row as fully-satisfied only once that fix has landed' - every one of these becomes FALSE the day po/dr-procedure merges. A customer-facing package that self-describes as pre-fix will go on telling customers the CA backup is world-readable after it no longer is. whitepaper:11-12 does say 're-review whenever any cited source materially changes', but compliance-officer correctly observed that this has no owner, no cadence and no mechanism - it is an aspiration, not a control. THREE AGENTS REACHED THIS INDEPENDENTLY FROM THREE DIRECTIONS, which is why independent_reporters is 2 for the compliance framing specifically and the convergence is worth naming: architect found no routed-concern row obliges these docs to be updated (arch5-6), enterprise-readiness found no ownership or drift-review obligation from the customer side (er5-1), and compliance-officer found the control-drift consequence. DISCHARGE, per compliance-officer: a .claude/routed-concerns.md row binding docs/assurance/** to docs-writer and compliance-officer on any change to a cited source, plus a named owner and a dated cadence.
classification_rationale: no update obligation exists for a customer-facing package whose assertions have a known expiry

trigger: An assessor attempts to TEST three of the control areas the matrix asserts; none states a testable assertion.

TESTABLE AND ADEQUATE: audit retention and export, RBAC, SSO/MFA, secrets-at-rest, CA custody, backup/restore, supply-chain verification. NOT TESTABLE, three: (a) VULNERABILITY MANAGEMENT at matrix:38 cites a Dependabot and OpenSSF-scorecard programme and sources it to docs/user-manual/release-verification.md, which has ZERO hits for either term - and there is no remediation-window commitment, so CC7.1's 'remediated timely' cannot be tested at all. This is pass-1's co-4, still open at HEAD. (b) MONITORING AND ALERT RESPONSE at matrix:32 is honestly caveated, but with no CI gate and no Alertmanager there is no testable alert-response control, while readiness:34 lists incident-notification SLAs as an ACCEPTED WS-A commitment - so the package promises a response capability in one place and disclaims its mechanism in another. (c) INCIDENT RESPONSE at matrix:36 marks Yuzu '—' and cites readiness section 3.4, whose Target State assigns runbooks and IR TO Yuzu. This is pass-1's co-5, still open. PROVENANCE IS pre-existing for all three and is recorded as such rather than charged to this change; what is new is that this change is the first to put them in front of a customer. trigger: An operator runs this branch's backup procedure; the CA root private key is written with no permission discipline, and the duty assigned in the matrix is unreachable from the procedure the operator actually executes.
summary: PARTIALLY CLOSED, AND THE HIGH TRAVELS TO po/dr-procedure AS A MERGE-BLOCKING CONDITION ON THAT PR. THIS IS A DE-ESCALATION ON THIS BRANCH AND IT IS ADJUDICATED BY AN AGENT OTHER THAN THE ONE THAT RAISED IT AT PASS 3-4, ON NEW EVIDENCE. What closed permanently: the pass-3 CRITICAL theory was that the row made a FALSE ASSERTION. It no longer does. matrix:20 and :25 now rate shared-responsibility, name the world-readable CA-key exposure explicitly, and assign the modes to the operator - and security-guardian VERIFIED the underlying disclosure is true, finding zero chmod and zero umask occurrences across scripts/yuzu-backup.sh, scripts/yuzu-restore.sh and docs/operations/disaster-recovery.md. Honest non-overclaiming disclosure is what the pass-3 finding asked for. WHAT REMAINS AND WHY IT IS NOT DISCHARGED HERE: disclosure is not discharge. The document that PERFORMS the backup - docs/operations/disaster-recovery.md, byte-identical to origin/dev on this branch - still contains no permission text, so the assigned duty is unreachable from the actor's own procedure and is therefore not an operating control under CC5.2 or CC6.1. compliance-officer's ruling, which the orchestrator records as the disposition: the FIX exists only in PR-B's copy of the file, so the HIGH travels to po/dr-procedure as a merge-blocking condition on THAT PR, and the residual on THIS branch is MEDIUM - pre-existing, honestly labelled, no false assurance. ONE CONDITION ATTACHES AND IT IS LOAD-BEARING: po/evidence must not merge ahead of po/dr-procedure without a dated, recorded exception, because the matrix's pre-fix language goes false the moment the DR PR lands (see co5-5). compliance-officer also explicitly separated UP5-11's indeterminacy concern from this row - that is co5-2's retrievability problem, not a second custody defect.
classification_rationale: supersession; band de-escalated on this branch by an independent adjudicator on new evidence, with the HIGH re-homed rather than dropped
adjudicated_by: compliance-officer (Gate 6, pass 5) - not the change author and not the agent that raised the finding at passes 3-4; separation applied is the de-escalation rule's
adjudication_rationale: The pass-3/4 CRITICAL-then-HIGH rested on the row making a FALSE ASSERTION about CA custody. security-guardian verified at Gate 2 that the row's disclosure is now factually TRUE (zero chmod/umask in all three DR artefacts), which removes the false-assertion basis entirely. The residual defect - that the assigned duty is unreachable from the procedure the operator runs - is real but lives wholly in docs/operations/disaster-recovery.md, which this branch carries byte-identical to origin/dev and does not modify. Under the operator's standing ruling that DR-procedure defects are reviewed on the stacked branch, the HIGH is re-homed to po/dr-procedure as a merge-blocking condition there rather than discharged; the MEDIUM residual recorded here reflects the honestly-labelled pre-existing exposure that remains on this branch. The finding is not dropped and its band is not lowered in aggregate - it is relocated to the PR that can fix it, with a merge-ordering condition attached.

trigger: Any overlay restart, rejected reload, or stray-.yml crash loop; the resulting zero-or-stale-rules state is not observed by any scrape job or any alert rule in this repo.
summary: THE MONITORING PLANE MONITORS EVERYTHING EXCEPT ITSELF, WHICH IS WHY EVERY FAILURE MODE THIS PASS FOUND IS STRUCTURALLY UNDETECTABLE. This is the finding that explains the others. prometheus-observability.yml defines exactly two scrape jobs, yuzu-server and yuzu-gateway. There is NO job_name: 'prometheus'. Prometheus's own instrumentation is therefore collected by nothing, and sre confirmed by grep across all 21 groups that docs/prometheus/yuzu-alerts.yml contains zero prometheus_* references. CONSEQUENCE: the three failure modes Gates 3, 4 and 5 established - the overlay not being sticky (win-start-UAT.sh:285 base-only, which sre confirmed directly), a rejected reload serving the stale set, and a stray .yml crash-looping the container - ALL present identically as zero-or-stale rules with the container Up and every target up, and NOTHING IN THIS REPO CAN SEE THAT STATE. The one-shot manual curl is the only detector, and UP5-8 already established it has no expiry. THE SPECIFIC CLOSE, which sre supplied rather than gesturing at: add `- job_name: 'prometheus'` with `static_configs: [{targets: ['localhost:9090']}]`, then alert on `sum(prometheus_rule_group_rules) < 116`, `prometheus_config_last_reload_successful == 0`, `increase(prometheus_rule_evaluation_failures_total[10m]) > 0`, `increase(prometheus_rule_group_iterations_missed_total[10m]) > 0`, plus a `Watchdog: expr: vector(1)` dead-man's switch. THE SPLIT sre proposed is the right one and matters for Gate 7: the SELF-SCRAPE JOB IS IN-PR - prometheus-observability.yml is created by this change and owned by it, and the addition is four lines - while the RULE GROUP is a follow-up, because yuzu-alerts.yml is explicitly outside this change's owned scope per the overlay header. Until the rule group lands, docs/uat-environment.md must name '0 rules loaded is silent' as a KNOWN UNDETECTABLE STATE rather than only prescribing a one-shot curl. FALSE ASSURANCE applies because uat-environment.md:38, added by this change, states the rules CAN be evaluated by a running Prometheus.
classification_rationale: the self-observation capability that would detect this change's own failure modes is absent; established by reading the scrape config and grepping the rule file

trigger: Any SLO attainment query over a 30-day window on a stack whose Prometheus runs the 15-day default retention.
summary: THE OPERATIONAL SIZING OF UP5-4, WITH NUMBERS, AND THE FINDING THAT THE OVERLAY IS THE ONLY FILE THAT CAN CARRY THE FIX. sre was asked to size UP5-4 rather than re-file it, and did. WHERE THE FIX MUST GO: the base docker-compose.uat.yml:14-23 has NO `command:` key at all, so the overlay REPLACES it wholesale - which means deploy/docker/docker-compose.observability.yml is the only file in the tree that can carry a retention flag for this rig. That is a fact Gate 4 did not have. DOES RETENTION INTERACT WITH ANYTHING ELSE? sre checked rather than assuming, and the answer is NO: the maximum `for:` duration in the rule set is 3h and pending state is in-memory; the largest range selector is [24h] with three uses and [3h] with thirteen; the recording rule is 10s-resolution. Fifteen days covers every rule comfortably. RETENTION BREAKS EXACTLY ONE THING - all five SLO windows - AND BREAKS THEM SILENTLY. THE NUMBERS, for the UAT rig with one server and one gateway, roughly 341 described server families plus 31 gateway, histogram and label fanout giving about 5,000 active series: 5,000 x 8,640 samples/day is 43.2M samples/day, at about 1.7 bytes per sample that is roughly 73 MB/day - so 15 days is about 1.1 GB, 30 days about 2.2 GB, and 40 days about 2.9 GB on the prometheus-uat-data named volume, against a Docker VM disk of 60 GB or more. sre's conclusion: THE FIX IS FREE. Recommended `--storage.tsdb.retention.time=40d`, being the 30-day window plus ten days of headroom. NECESSARY BUT NOT SUFFICIENT, and sre flagged this itself: even at 40d, a rig booted less than 30 days ago returns a partial avg_over_time(...[30d]) that is still indistinguishable from a full one, so slo.md additionally needs a stated 'window not yet full' precondition alongside its existing 'not yet baselined'.
classification_rationale: the retention setting required by the document's own measurement windows is absent, and the overlay is the only file that can supply it

trigger: The overlay is presented as the mechanism that makes the shipped alert rules real, while the rig's own launcher silently returns it to zero rules and no self-observation exists to detect that.
summary: REOPENED AT GATE 6 BY THE AGENT THAT CLOSED IT AT GATE 3, ON ITS OWN MOTION, ON EVIDENCE THAT DID NOT EXIST WHEN IT CLOSED IT. THIS IS A STRENGTHENING SUPERSESSION - the gate becomes harder to pass, not easier - so no de-escalation attestation is required, and the orchestrator records it prominently because a reviewer withdrawing its own closure is the rarest and most valuable event this pipeline produces. sre's reasoning, preserved: it closed sre6-5 at Gate 3 on the HONESTY OF THE QUALIFICATION, and it confirms that judgement still stands on its own terms - slo.md:294-303 does still say the claim is 'these rules exist and parse' rather than 'evaluated by a live system', and that text survives. WHAT IT DID NOT HAVE AT GATE 3 IS UP5-7. scripts/win-start-UAT.sh:285 runs base-only `docker compose -f docker-compose.uat.yml up -d`, which sre confirmed directly for itself rather than taking Gate 4's word. Combined with sre6p5-2's finding that no self-scrape job exists, this is a monitoring plane that can reach ZERO RULES WITH NO OPERATOR MISTAKE AND STAY THERE INVISIBLY, on the repo's own launcher - while docs/uat-environment.md:38, added by THIS change, states the rules 'can be evaluated by a running Prometheus', and the shipped verification is a one-shot manual curl with no expiry, no re-run contract and no teardown instruction. sre's conclusion in its own words: that combination is exactly the gap sre6-5 names, reached by a path nobody had evidence for at Gate 3; closing it was premature. VERDICT: the observability story is NOT ready to be described the way the assurance documents describe it. sre also noted both blockers are cheap - one flag and about 3 GB for sre6p5-1, four lines of scrape config for sre6p5-2 - and neither requires C++ or a new store.
classification_rationale: supersession reopening a prior closure on new evidence; strengthens the gate, so no de-escalation attestation applies

trigger: The auth store closes AFTER boot; /readyz returns 503, /health returns 200 with status degraded, and up{job=yuzu-server} still reads 1.
summary: THE POST-BOOT DEGRADE CLASS HAS NO METRIC, NO ALERT AND NO RUNBOOK ROW, SO ITS MEAN TIME TO DETECTION IS 'A HUMAN REPORTS LOGIN FAILURES'. sre established that no yuzu_server_store_open-style gauge exists anywhere (grep: zero hits), so the /readyz conjunction - about thirty store checks - is exported to no metric at all. Meanwhile auth-db-recovery.md:31-45's ENTIRE 'Detection signal' table consists of BOOT-TIME LOG LINES: every row describes a server that refused to start. The class where the server is already up and the auth store closes afterwards has no row, no alert and no metric, and it presents as /readyz 503, /health 200-with-degraded, and up == 1 - which is UP5-16's finding arriving from the recovery-runbook side. sre noted the rule set documents the SIBLING shape repeatedly, at yuzu-alerts.yml:2692, :2716 and :2746, all describing how /readyz stays green under pool saturation, while nothing covers the inverse. AT 3AM THE OPERATOR HAS no page, no dashboard delta, and a runbook whose first diagnostic step assumes the process is dead. NATIVE-VS-DERIVED DISAGREEMENT, which sre reported itself: it labelled this HIGH on the ground that unbounded MTTD on a security-control surface is severe, then derived MEDIUM because the false-assurance half is already filed as UP5-16 and double-counting it here would inflate the aggregate. The derived band governs and the orchestrator endorses the restraint. THE SPLIT: exporting the /readyz conjunction as yuzu_server_ready or per-store yuzu_server_store_open{store}, alerting == 0 for 2m, is SERVER-SIDE C++ work and is a follow-up; the RUNBOOK ROW documenting the post-boot degrade class is free and belongs in this change.
classification_rationale: a detection signal and its runbook row are absent for a failure class the same package's SLO section depends on

trigger: Every rig start; three alerts fire on a cold boot and no document records what the expected steady-state alert set is.
summary: THE SRE JUDGEMENT NOBODY ELSE COULD MAKE: THREE ALERTS ON A COLD BOOT IS CORRECT BEHAVIOUR, NOT A NOISE PROBLEM - AND THE REAL DEFECT IS ADJACENT AND WORSE. sre was asked whether a rig that alerts on three rules the moment it starts is a usable baseline or a noise problem that trains operators to ignore alerts, and it ruled clearly: each of the three is TRUE. The native server genuinely is not running, and the absent()-guarded counters at yuzu-alerts.yml:1273 and :2343 genuinely have never been seeded. A 116-rule set producing three true alerts against an empty fleet is a GOOD signal-to-noise ratio and sre would not expect an operator to learn to ignore it. THE ACTUAL DEFECT: the shipped verification counts RULES, not ALERT STATE, and no document records what the expected steady-state alert set IS. So an operator cannot distinguish three-expected from four-real - which is precisely the mechanism by which a real alert does get ignored. The noise problem is not present; the inability to tell noise from signal is. FIX, which also answers HP5-3's half: record the expected cold-boot alert names in docs/uat-environment.md, and replace the count assertion with a health assertion - `curl -s localhost:9090/api/v1/rules | jq '[.data.groups[].rules[]|select(.health!="ok")]'` - because HP5-3 is right that a rule count is the wrong check.
classification_rationale: the expected steady-state alert set is undocumented, so the shipped verification cannot distinguish expected from real

trigger: The overlay makes evaluation_interval load-bearing for the first time; at production label fanout the 13 [3h] and 3 [24h] rules at a 10s interval become the dominant CPU consumer.
summary: evaluation_interval: 10s IS NEWLY LOAD-BEARING AND IS SIX TIMES THE PROMETHEUS DEFAULT FOR NO STATED REASON. sre made the observation that before this change NO RULES LOADED, so evaluation_interval was inert - this PR is what turns it into the multiplier on all rule CPU. THE COST AT UAT SCALE, measured rather than asserted: 116 rules across 21 groups, with groups evaluated in parallel and rules serially within a group, at roughly 1-3 ms per rule on a 5,000-series TSDB, gives 0.12 to 0.35 seconds per cycle against a 10-second interval - so 1.2% to 3.5% of one core, plus ALERTS and ALERTS_FOR_STATE series churn at 10s. NEGLIGIBLE HERE, and this is also sre's answer to the capacity question the gate asked: the overlay's capacity cost is real but trivial on the UAT rig, and the 15-day default retention is a CORRECTNESS problem rather than a disk problem. THE FORWARD RISK: at production fanout, with per-agent labels over a ten-thousand-device fleet giving 10^5 to 10^6 series, those 13 [3h] and 3 [24h] rules evaluated every 10 seconds become the dominant consumer. RECOMMENDATION: decouple evaluation_interval from scrape_interval and set it to 30-60s before any production profile inherits this file - which matters because the overlay's own header proposes extending the same pattern to full-uat.
classification_rationale: a newly load-bearing tuning parameter carries no rationale and no production guidance

trigger: superseded - see summary
summary: ADJUDICATED: happy-path's EVIDENCE IS CORRECT ON ALL FOUR STEPS AND sre WITHDRAWS ITS GATE 3 POSITION; happy-path's ROUTING IS WRONG, SO THE FINDING TRAVELS. sre was asked to adjudicate its own Gate 3 'sound' assessment against happy-path's handler-level evidence, and it verified each step against the handlers rather than the prose. STEP 1: /health computes status as healthy-or-degraded at server.cpp:13553 and then calls res.set_content at :13586 with NO res.status assignment, so it returns HTTP 200 and `curl -fsS` succeeds on a fully degraded server - CONFIRMED. STEP 2: prints schema_meta.version with no expected value stated anywhere in the runbook - CONFIRMED. STEP 3: the metric is yuzu_server_secret_decrypt_failures_total, emitted only inside a loop over kek_enrolled_codecs() at server.cpp:7989-7997, and describe() alone does not export a series - the file says so itself at :2570-2577 - so on a CORRECT restore the series is absent and grep exits 1; the prose mitigates a reader but not a set -e paste - CONFIRMED. Under the operator's ruling that DR-procedure defects belong to po/dr-procedure, the routing is there. sre's summary is the fair one: both partly right - happy-path's evidence is correct, its routing is not. ONE CARRY-OVER THE STACKED BRANCH MUST NOT MISS, and sre flagged it specifically: the disclaimer at :525-529 scopes itself to docs/operations/disaster-recovery.md, but the DEFECTIVE BLOCK PHYSICALLY LIVES IN auth-db-recovery.md:205-230 - so the stacked PR must fix THIS copy, not only the DR page it was cited from.
classification_rationale: supersession to split following an independent adjudication that upheld the evidence and corrected the routing

trigger: An operator follows the new guidance exactly, then performs a routine restart using the command the rig's own docs give, and lands at zero evaluated rules with no way to tell.
summary: THE THREE NEW WARNINGS ARE SCOPED TO THE WRONG FAILURE MODE - THIS IS THE DOCUMENTATION HALF OF UP5-7 AND IS NOT A RE-FILE. enterprise-readiness observed that all three new warning sites - the overlay header at :20-30, the new section in docs/uat-environment.md, and the readiness doc's WS-D entry - warn at length and CORRECTLY about the -f ORDER hazard. NONE of them warns that a later base-only `docker compose -f docker-compose.uat.yml up -d`, which is the command the rig's own documentation gives for routine restarts, drops the overlay and returns Prometheus to zero rules, healthy and green. So an operator who follows the new guidance EXACTLY still lands at zero evaluated rules and cannot tell. THE CONSEQUENCE FOR THE READINESS DOC, which answers the gate's item 8 directly: WS-D's 'verified live this pass' attests to the ORDER hazard while the STICKINESS hazard goes entirely unstated, so the WS-D observability status does NOT fully match what ships. Recorded as I7 - a required doc absent for security-relevant behaviour, namely the silent loss of all alert evaluation - rather than as a second copy of UP5-7's I6, so the two are not double-counted. FIX: state in all three places that the overlay is NOT sticky and that every subsequent up -d must repeat both -f flags, and make the /api/v1/rules assertion a POST-RESTART step rather than a one-time one.
classification_rationale: the warning for the actual dominant failure mode is absent from all three sites that warn about the lesser one

trigger: A customer making a production monitoring decision reads the matrix's monitoring row, whose lead clause advertises 115 shipped alert rules; the production reference compose ships no Prometheus at all.
summary: THE MONITORING ROW OMITS THE OPERATOR'S SINGLE LARGEST MONITORING DUTY, AND BURIES THE DISCLAIMER BEHIND THE ADVERTISEMENT. The Operator column says 'Wire an Alertmanager' but never says DEPLOY A PROMETHEUS - and enterprise-readiness verified that docker-compose.reference.yml contains zero prometheus and zero grafana occurrences, so a production pilot gets no scrape, no evaluation and no alerting from this change whatsoever. The disclaimer does exist, but it sits at the END of a roughly 150-word cell behind a leading '◐ Ships 115 Prometheus alert rules', and a customer making a monitoring decision reads the lead. This is the pilot-visible consequence of the overlay being UAT-only, expressed as a customer-assurance defect rather than a deployment one. enterprise-readiness derived I6 - the capability is unreachable in the shipped production template - and was careful to state why it is NOT false assurance: the row does not claim alerts are in force, so nothing is advertised as enforced that is not. FIX: lead the cell with 'UAT rig only - the production reference compose ships no Prometheus', and add 'stand up and operate a Prometheus' as the FIRST Operator-column duty, ahead of the Alertmanager.
classification_rationale: the cell's lead clause and its buried disclaimer point a customer in opposite directions on a production decision

trigger: Any change to a fact the assurance package restates - the rule count, a default flag, the TLS posture, an SLO target - with no obligation on anyone to update the package.
summary: NO OWNERSHIP, REVISION OR DRIFT-REVIEW OBLIGATION ON THE REPO'S FIRST CUSTOMER-FACING ASSURANCE PACKAGE. The 116-rule count, the four-defaults table, the TLS posture and the SLO targets are each duplicated across two to four files, with a hand-maintained 'Last updated' line as the ONLY integrity signal, and architect confirmed at Gate 3 that no routed-concern row obliges an update. THE CUSTOMER CONSEQUENCE enterprise-readiness named, which is sharper than the process observation: a whitepaper that silently goes stale between releases while still asserting 'no cell asserts a control this repo does not actually implement' - so the document's own integrity claim degrades into exactly the overclaim it was written to avoid. That is the mechanism by which an honest document becomes a dishonest one without anyone editing it. THREE AGENTS REACHED THIS INDEPENDENTLY FROM THREE DIRECTIONS at two different gates: architect from module boundaries (arch5-6), compliance-officer from control drift (co5-5), and enterprise-readiness from customer assurance. None was shown the others' findings. That convergence is why independent_reporters is 3 and why this is the most durable improvement available from pass 5. DISCHARGE, combining all three proposals: add a routed-concern row binding docs/assurance/** to server.hpp defaults, docs/pki-architecture.md, docs/prometheus/yuzu-alerts.yml and slo.md; name a document owner; and make the whitepaper a release-gated artefact re-verified at tag time.
classification_rationale: no update obligation, owner or cadence exists for a package whose accuracy claim is its entire value

trigger: An operator who hand-wired the deleted deploy/grafana/yuzu-alerts.yml upgrades; seven detections are retired with no upgrade note, no successor and no filed issue.
summary: SEVEN RETIRED DETECTIONS HAVE NO OPERATOR UPGRADE NOTE AND NO FILED SUCCESSOR ISSUE. enterprise-readiness credited the retirement table in the readiness doc as exemplary, then made the point only it would make: that table lives in an INTERNAL GRC PLANNING DOCUMENT that no operator reads on upgrade, and docs/user-manual/ gains nothing at all. Derived I7 with NO escalation, and enterprise-readiness was explicit about why: the removal is tabled in-repo, so it is not CONCEALED - it is merely in the wrong document for its audience. EXPOSURE E4 because nothing in-repo referenced the file, so only a hand-wiring operator is affected. FIX: file the seven successor issues and add an upgrade note under docs/user-manual/.
