trigger: A5 exception ledger entry #2990 had its exposure widened on 2026-08-11 when the fallback path became default-reachable, without its revisit-by date being pulled forward.
summary: THE A5 EXCEPTION LEDGER PASSES HYGIENE WITH ONE REAL DATING DEFECT. enterprise-readiness audited all five entries: every one carries a surface, a waived item and an issue number; four are closed with issue references (#2436, #2712, #2986, #2439); and the single OPEN entry, #2990, has a live revisit-by of 2026-10-31, which is NOT stale as at today's date of 2026-09-11. So the ledger is clean on the standard checks and that is recorded as a clean result. THE DEFECT IT FOUND INSTEAD is subtler and is the kind only a careful read surfaces: that open entry records that its exposure was WIDENED on 2026-08-11 - the fallback path became default-reachable on every deployment via PR #2987, unmetered, with only a coarse kill switch - and the revisit-by date was NOT pulled forward to match. A widened waiver retaining its pre-widening review date is a real hygiene failure, because the review cadence was set against a narrower exposure than the one now in force. SEPARATELY: the WS-G bullet instructs disclosing this residual to technical reviewers, but security-whitepaper.md section 8 says only 'Track 2f's Phase 3 remains planned' - so the disclosure obligation the workstream accepted is not met in the document that faces the reviewer. Per arch5-1 this change owes NO NEW LEDGER ENTRY, so this is hygiene of the existing ledger only. FIX: pull #2990's revisit-by forward on exposure widening, and mirror the residual into whitepaper section 8.
classification_rationale: a waiver's review cadence no longer matches the exposure it governs; the accepted disclosure obligation is unmet in the customer-facing document

trigger: A prospective customer is sent the assurance package today; six control families it describes are absent from v0.13.0, the only release they can obtain, and the package never states v0.13.0's actual posture.
summary: THE CUSTOMER-ASSURANCE RULING ON UP5-12: ANCHORING AN ASSURANCE DOCUMENT TO AN UNRELEASABLE COMMIT IS NOT ACCEPTABLE EVEN WITH DISCLOSURE. enterprise-readiness was asked for an explicit ruling and gave one, CONCURRING with unhappy-path's HIGH from an independent direction - so this is recorded as its own row with independent_reporters 2 rather than folded into UP5-12. ITS REASONING, which adds the decisive argument Gate 4 did not have: disclosure fixes ATTRIBUTION, not USABILITY. The whitepaper tells a reviewer that six control families are absent from v0.13.0 but NEVER STATES WHAT v0.13.0's POSTURE IS - so for the only build a customer can actually obtain, the document answers no question at all. And it is made worse by this same change: auth-db-recovery.md now proves the two builds require OPPOSITE emergency actions, so the package describes a security posture that no procurable artefact has. WHAT TO SEND TODAY, which is the operational output of the ruling: nothing from docs/assurance/ until either a release is cut at or after this anchor, or the whitepaper gains a per-section 'v0.13.0 posture' column; in the interim send only sections 1, 2.2 and 6, which are true in both builds. THE BROADER ASSESSMENT this sits inside, recorded because it is the judgement only this agent could make: the package is NOT YET fit to send but is CLOSE, and its unusual honesty - per-hop TLS disaggregated rather than claimed uniformly, 'tamper-evident' explicitly retracted, the four permissive defaults tabled with their exact flip flags - reads as RIGOUR to a technical reviewer and as IMMATURITY to procurement. enterprise-readiness's recommendation is audience separation rather than softening: keep this whitepaper verbatim for technical due diligence, add a short procurement-facing summary, and do not dilute section 3.8.
classification_rationale: the package describes a posture no obtainable build has, and never states the posture of the build a customer can get

summary: THE CUSTOMER-ASSURANCE DOMAIN OWNER DISSENTS FROM UP5-11's HIGH AND DERIVES LOW, AND ITS REASONING IS THE STRONGEST ON EITHER SIDE. enterprise-readiness was asked to give its own derivation rather than echo, and it did. ITS DERIVATION: the conditional resolves DETERMINISTICALLY to shared-responsibility for every reader who is not the Yuzu team, because the fix has by construction not landed in the procedure they run - so the reader CAN tell, which defeats I3. And the named operator action - umask 077, 0700, 0600 - is stated three times in the row and is the SAFE action, which defeats I4. That leaves I8, degraded-but-correct, with E0, deriving LOW. THE INSIGHT IT ADDS THAT BOTH OTHER POSITIONS MISSED: the harm is not indeterminacy at all - it is that the row tells the customer to WAIT FOR AN EVENT THEY CANNOT OBSERVE. That is a better description of the defect than either the HIGH or the clean verdict, and it yields a cleaner fix: delete the conditional, state the row as shared-responsibility unconditionally, and keep the operator duty. THE FULL TALLY ON THIS FINDING, recorded by the orchestrator for operator adjudication and NOT re-adjudicated here: unhappy-path derived HIGH; security-guardian derived LOW (sec5-5); happy-path derived LOW (HP5-7); consistency-auditor found the labelling CLEAN across all eight citations; and enterprise-readiness, the domain owner for customer assurance, derives LOW. That is four positions at LOW-or-clean against one at HIGH. The orchestrator does not collapse them - Gate 6b records the maximum derived band as provisional per the synthesis rule - but flags this as THE single band on pass 5 most warranting an operator ruling, and notes that the Gate 4 row's characterisation of HP5-7 as converging on the HIGH was the orchestrator's error and is corrected here.
classification_rationale: an independent derivation by the domain owner, dissenting from a peer's band on the same facts; recorded alongside rather than resolved

FIXED by 6a9b4e5ce, confirmed independently by execution at Gate 3. UP4-4 held that the rig could never pick up a rules change while running, because --web.enable-lifecycle appeared nowhere in the repo, so `curl -XPOST :9090/-/reload` returned 'Lifecycle API is not enabled' and the overlay's stated purpose was false for every post-start edit. The flag is now set at deploy/docker/docker-compose.observability.yml:102. release-deploy verified the consequence rather than the presence: an unauthenticated POST /-/reload against the running overlay returns 200. RESIDUALS, recorded so this closure is not read as more than it is: sec5-3 finds the documented reload has no -f or status check and that a REJECTED reload leaves the previous rule set loaded while the count still reads 116; sec5-2 and R5-5 find the same flag exposes an unauthenticated /-/quit on a port the base rig publishes on 0.0.0.0. The reload capability UP4-4 asked for exists; what rides along with it is new and is filed separately.

FIXED by 6a9b4e5ce. UP4-5 held that the rules mount was a single-file bind, so rename-replace edits would pin the container to the old inode and a reload would keep serving stale content. The mount is now a DIRECTORY bind - `../../docs/prometheus:/etc/prometheus/rules:ro` at docker-compose.observability.yml:105 - which is the correct fix and resolves the inode-pinning mechanism. TWO QUALIFICATIONS ARE RECORDED RATHER THAN GLOSSED. First, the evidence strength: sre established at Gate 6, when asked directly, that of the three overlay fixes this is the one that was REASONED, not executed - the overlay's own header says so verbatim at :76-77 ('reproduced by reasoning from documented Docker bind-mount semantics, not independently re-executed here'). doc5-F3 and C5-1 both find that two OTHER documents nevertheless describe all three as 'verified live', which overstates this one. Second, the directory mount introduced a NEW defect that did not exist under the single-file bind: R5-2 and arch5-4 find that the `*.yml` glob over docs/prometheus/ means any future non-rules .yml dropped there crash-loops Prometheus under restart: unless-stopped, taking down the whole rule set - release-deploy reproduced that by execution. The fix is correct; its blast radius changed shape.

FIXED IN SUBSTANCE by 6a9b4e5ce, AND THE REMEDIATION INTRODUCED A NEW BLOCKING DEFECT - both facts recorded, neither hidden behind the other. UP4-9 held that auth-db-recovery.md's session-revocation correction was version-unqualified and therefore FALSE for v0.13.0, the latest tagged release, because it gave the dev-HEAD answer unconditionally and would have told a v0.13.0 operator to abandon their fastest emergency tool. The version qualification now exists: the runbook distinguishes the durable-session build from v0.13.0 and states the opposite, correct emergency action for each, with `git cat-file -e v0.13.0:server/core/src/session_store.hpp` cited as the evidence that the header is absent in that release. That substance is addressed and this finding closes on it. WHAT THE FIX BROKE, which is why this closure is paired with an explicit pointer rather than left clean: the MECHANISM the fix offers an operator to determine which side of the boundary they are on is defective three separate ways - sec5-1 and doc5-F1 found the discriminator query names `session_store.schema_meta`, a relation existing on NEITHER build, with its failure branch resolving to the dangerous answer; UP5-1 found the query is a Postgres query invoked in a runbook whose own subject includes Postgres being unreachable, so a connection failure is indistinguishable from a missing relation; and UP5-3 found the stated `--version` fallback names no version boundary and cannot express one under this project's plain-X.Y.Z convention. sec5-1 carries a policy floor as the false-green closure evidence for THIS finding. A separate supersession on sec5-1 records caused_by: UP4-9 so the causal chain is queryable.

caused_by: UP4-9 - this defect was introduced by the pass-5 remediation of UP4-9 (the version-qualification fix), whose build-discriminator mechanism it is

summary: THE BUILD DISCRIMINATOR IS THE SAME DEFECT IN A NEW SHAPE: IT READS TRUE AND IS FALSE. Step 2 tells the operator to run `journalctl -u yuzu-server | grep -i session_store` and states 'its presence means the durable build, its absence means legacy'. A SUCCESSFUL DURABLE BOOT EMITS NO SUCH LINE. security-guardian enumerated every string literal containing session_store and every spdlog call mentioning a session across server/core/src/*.cpp: the ONLY boot-path emitter is server.cpp:4227-4229, INSIDE `if (!session_store_->is_open())`, which also sets startup_failed_.
